description: Controlled vocabulary defining canonical entity classes permitted within the A.R.I.A. Knowledge Graph.

entity_types.description: Manufacturer of telecommunications equipment, software, tools, or supporting systems.
Customer, carrier, contractor, or other organization relevant to technical or operational context.
Individual participating in operational, technical, diagnostic, or historical experience.
Functional role performed by a person or system.
Manufacturer-defined or technically meaningful family of related products.
Canonical telecommunications product or equipment platform.
Distinct variant of a canonical product requiring independent technical applicability.
Hardware revision or generation affecting technical applicability.
Physical component forming part of a larger telecommunications system.
Physical or logical connection interface.
Specific physical or logical equipment port.
Microwave or telecommunications antenna.
Radio-frequency telecommunications equipment.
Component participating in an RF signal path.
Frequency band or range relevant to telecommunications operation.
RF polarization state or configuration.
Frequency channel or channel assignment.
Modulation mode, modulation order, or adaptive modulation state.
Network, radio, protection, or equipment topology.
Canonical configuration state, mode, option, or technical setting.
Individual configurable parameter.
Canonical value applicable to a configuration parameter.
Firmware release or firmware family.
Software application, management system, or software platform.
Specific software version or release.
Observable problem or abnormal condition initiating or contributing to diagnosis.
Technical manner in which a component, configuration, or system can fail.
Canonical underlying cause capable of producing one or more symptoms or failure modes.
Condition contributing to a failure without necessarily representing the primary root cause.
Canonical equipment or system alarm.
Diagnostic test capable of producing evidence.
Defined technical or operational procedure.
Action intended to correct a confirmed or suspected technical problem.
Canonical measurable technical quantity.
Canonical unit of measurement.
Technical threshold, tolerance, limit, or boundary.
Physical diagnostic, installation, test, or measurement tool.
Environmental condition capable of affecting installation, operation, measurement, or diagnosis.
Physical obstruction affecting line of sight, Fresnel clearance, installation, or RF propagation.
Type or scope of technical work.
Project or deployment lifecycle phase.
Engineering, regulatory, customer, manufacturer, or internal technical standard.
Canonical technical, operational, safety, regulatory, or customer requirement.
Condition limiting valid configurations, actions, designs, or procedures.
Technical concept that does not belong to a more specific canonical entity type.
